item.title: Comment on Lesson 1: Image and Emotion: Pablo Neruda and the Power of Metaphor by Gaelle Petit-Homme
item.description: There it stood at my doorstep, cocky and proud. Growing by the minute, A confident smirk graces the mysterious silhouette, With three knocks, it demands access, I hesitantly open with teary eyes, I unwillingly let it in, knowing it's here to stay. It engulfs me in one take, My heart quivers in my chest. I'll have to adapt to this pain.

item.title: Comment on Lesson 1: Image and Emotion: Pablo Neruda and the Power of Metaphor by Gaelle Petit-Homme
item.description: I think giving that emotion such characteristics allows me to personify it more. It doesn't surprise me, I've envisioned it this way before. It would be a great antagonist in a story, a great metaphor in poems.

item.title: Comment on Creating a Productive Study Space &amp; Gathering Materials by Kayla Martinez
item.description: Definitely agree with Lili about wanting some space to pace- I always end up needing to move around when I'm working stories out. I would also love a lot of natural lighting- warm lamps are a great idea I never thought of though! I'd also love a bulletin board so I can put up my character drawings, outlines, etc. I'd love a big desk, with a big organizer beside it so I can keep all my art supplies out, and just shove 'em in a drawer somewhere and forget I have 'em. :)

item.title: Comment on Maintaining a Productive Study Space &amp; Summary by Kayla Martinez
item.description: I would love to clean up my kitchen table a bit and work there (lots of natural light there as opposed to the desk in my room). Also, I think my sister might already have a bulletin board I can borrow.

item.title: Comment on Setting Smart Goals by Kayla Martinez
item.description: I want to finish the second draft of my novel, so I will dedicate a day every week to rewriting 3 chapters.

item.title: Comment on Visualization &amp; Reflection by Kayla Martinez
item.description: When I visualize my goal for this journey, I'm presenting a small excerpt from my novel to my lovely journey community members. Hopefully, I'm sharing my screen and showing them a few complementary visual elements as well. When I visualize my ultimate goal of publishing my first book, I'm holding the finished product complete with illustrations and comics. item.title: Comment on Scheduling Tips by Kayla Martinez
item.description: I build my calendar pretty much entirely through a physical planner. I've tried color coding tasks before and really enjoyed it, but I've fallen out of the habit. Typically I'll just make a list of things I wanna work on and switch between or I'll plan out how much time I wanna spend working on something. For example, I have "GWN (1 hour)" down for this. I'll really just write the hard deadline in on my planner in all caps. I wanna try experimenting with giving myself soft deadlines though.

item.title: Comment on Fostering a Procrastination-Free Space by Kayla Martinez
item.description: Keep my many knick-knacks well organized or out of site. Try not to have excessive stacks of books, sketchbooks, notebooks that aren't relevant to the work I'm doing. Keep some water next to me so I don't forget to hydrate. Tell my family when I'm doing work so they know not to come in and ask me to do something.

item.title: Comment on Overcoming Procrastination by Kayla Martinez
item.description: I love the idea of having a small break or reward after every work session or task completed. Seems like a great way to eliminate the habit of avoiding a giant block of work time.
